# qatalyst-commit-message

Used by `qatalyst-ticket-ship` (step 4, right after the token report) and `qatalyst-ticket-start`
(step 5, when the developer picks "Stop here, I'll commit later"). You write the message and let the
developer rework it; you never run `git commit` yourself. `qatalyst-ticket-ship` does that, with the
message this skill leaves behind.

## What you read

- The ticket ID, its type (bug or feature) and its Jira summary.
- For each repo touched: `git diff` against the ticket branch's base, and `git status` for new
  files. Describe only what the diff shows.
- `specs/<bug|feature>/<ticket ID>/tasks.md`: the tasks, and its `**Tests:**` line.
- For a bug, `log-analysis.md`: the confirmed root cause. Use the cause and the fix, never log
  lines.

## The message

**Title** (one line, 72 characters or fewer, no trailing full stop):

```
<ticket ID> - <imperative summary of the change>
```

For example `ABC-123 - Retry BLE bonding before discovering services`. The title always starts with
the ticket ID, a space, a hyphen and a space, whatever pattern the repo's older commits used. Say what the change does for the user or the code, not
how it was done ("Fix", "Add", "Stop", "Retry", not "Update code").

**Body** (after a blank line, wrapped at 72 characters):

1. One or two sentences on **why**: for a bug, the root cause in plain words; for a feature, what it
   lets the user do.
2. A short bullet list of **what changed**, grouped by task from `tasks.md`, not one bullet per
   file. Three to six bullets; fewer for a one-task ticket.
3. Tests, one line: what was added, or "No tests written for this change (developer's choice at
   approval)" when `tasks.md` says `**Tests:** none`. If tests weren't run before the commit, say
   that too ("Tests were not run locally.").
4. Anything a reviewer of this commit must know, one line each, only when it applies: review comments
   still open because the developer chose to commit anyway, and a "Fix check" finding in `tasks.md`
   (the finding, and that the developer chose to go ahead).
5. Nothing else. No file lists, no sign-off, and no `Co-Authored-By` or "generated by" trailer.

A change too small for a body (a one-line fix with an obvious title) gets the title alone. Don't pad
it.

## Rules

- Write only what the diff, `tasks.md` and `log-analysis.md` support. Never invent a cause, a
  benefit or a test that isn't there.
- Never put a token, JWT, email, phone number, device ID or other personal data in the message, even
  if the diff or a log has one.
- Several repos: one message per repo, each describing only that repo's diff. Don't mention the
  other repo's changes in it.
- Don't repeat the title in the body, and don't restate the Jira ticket's description.

## Saving it

Write the messages to `.logs/<ticket ID>/commit-message.md` (git-ignored), one section per repo:

```markdown
## <repo name>
Files: <path>, <path>, ...
Status: draft | approved

<title>

<body>
```

`Files:` lists the paths in that repo's diff, so a later run can tell whether the message still
fits. Set `Status: approved` only when the developer picks "Use this message". Rewrite the file on
every rework. The file's full path is given to the developer each time the message is shown.

## Showing it, and reworking it

Show every repo's message in full, as a fenced block with the title on the first line, so it can be
copied as it is. Then ask (see `qatalyst-ask-developer`):

| Option | What you do |
|---|---|
| Use this message | Mark every section `approved` and stop. |
| Make it shorter | Rewrite as the title and at most one body sentence. |
| Add more detail | Keep the title; add the reasoning behind the main choices and any risk worth a reviewer's attention, still only from the diff and `tasks.md`. |
| Change it (**needs text**) | Apply what they typed, whether a new title, a different style or a change to one repo's message. A change to one repo leaves the others as they were. |

After every rework, show the new message and ask again. Keep going until they pick "Use this
message"; they decide when it is done. If the developer's text asks for something the rules above
forbid (a log excerpt, a secret), say why you left it out and offer the rest.

## Two ways in

- **Called by `qatalyst-ticket-ship` ("Commit it now").** Run it at step 4, after the review and the
  token report, so the diff is final. Reuse a section that is already `approved` when its `Files:` line
  still matches the repo's current diff; write a fresh draft for any repo whose files changed, and
  say so. `qatalyst-ticket-ship` commits with the approved message.
- **Called by `qatalyst-ticket-start` ("Stop here, I'll commit later").** Run it once, on the diff as
  it stands, and end with the same question. Then say that `/qatalyst-ticket-ship` will reuse an
  approved message, and that they may also copy it for their own commit. Nothing is committed.
